chapters.title: Geographical Diversity of India
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: The Himalayas
objectives: Student can locate the Himalayas on a map and explain why they are like a massive wall with peaks over 8000 m
Student can explain how the Himalayas formed when the Indian landmass, which broke away from Gondwana, collided with Eurasia
Student can explain how snowmelt from the Himalayas feeds rivers such as the Ganga, Indus and Brahmaputra
visualIdeas: a physical map with the Himalayan range highlighted
a carpet wrinkling as it is pushed, compared with colliding landmasses

topics.title: The Cold Desert of India
objectives: Student can describe Ladakh as a cold desert with very low winter temperatures, little rain and rugged terrain
Student can name wildlife of Ladakh and explain why yaks are important to people in the Himalayas
visualIdeas: a rocky Ladakh landscape with Pangong Tso

topics.title: The Gangetic Plains
objectives: Student can explain why the Gangetic Plains are fertile and important for agriculture and civilisation
Student can explain why a large share of India's population lives in the plains and how the flat land helps transport networks
visualIdeas: rivers flowing from the Himalayas across the plains

topics.title: The Great Indian Desert or Thar Desert
objectives: Student can describe the Thar Desert, how wind shapes sand dunes, and the states it spans
Student can explain how people in the Thar have adapted their food, clothing and lifestyle to harsh conditions
visualIdeas: sand dunes being shaped by wind arrows

topics.title: The Aravalli Hills
objectives: Student can describe the Aravallis as among the oldest mountains in the world and trace the states they span
Student can explain how the Aravallis act as a natural barrier against the eastward spread of the Thar Desert and are rich in minerals
visualIdeas: the Aravalli range on a map between the Thar Desert and Delhi

topics.title: The Peninsular Plateau
objectives: Student can define a plateau and describe the triangular Peninsular Plateau bordered by the Western and Eastern Ghats
Student can describe the Deccan Plateau and rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri that flow across it from west to east
visualIdeas: a triangular plateau with the Western and Eastern Ghats on its sides

topics.title: India's Amazing Coastlines
objectives: Student can compare the West Coast (estuaries, Western Ghats rivers) and the East Coast (wide plains and deltas)
Student can define a delta and a lagoon with examples like Chilika and Pulicat
visualIdeas: a map of India's coastline with deltas and estuaries marked

topics.title: Indian Islands
objectives: Student can compare Lakshadweep (coral islands in the Arabian Sea) with the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (volcanic islands in the Bay of Bengal)
Student can explain the strategic and historical importance of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
visualIdeas: two island groups on either side of the peninsula

topics.title: The Delta in West Bengal and the Sundarbans
objectives: Student can describe the Sundarbans in the delta of the Ganga and Brahmaputra, shared with Bangladesh and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger
Student can locate the Sundarbans delta on a map and explain why it is a unique combination of river, sea and land
visualIdeas: a mangrove delta with a tiger

topics.title: The Hills of the Northeast
objectives: Student can describe the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills of the Meghalaya Plateau and their very high rainfall
Student can explain how India's diverse geography shapes life, economy and culture
visualIdeas: green hills with waterfalls and heavy rain clouds

chapters.title: Understanding the Weather
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Weather and its Elements
objectives: Student can define weather as the state of the atmosphere at a particular time and place
Student can describe the troposphere as the layer of the atmosphere where almost all weather occurs
Student can describe how people read nature's clues to predict the weather
visualIdeas: a layered cake of the atmosphere with the troposphere at the bottom

topics.title: Weather Instruments: Temperature and Precipitation
objectives: Student can explain how temperature is measured with a thermometer and recognise the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales
Student can explain how a rain gauge measures rainfall in millimetres
visualIdeas: a thermometer next to a rain gauge with a funnel and scale

topics.title: Weather Instruments: Atmospheric Pressure and Wind
objectives: Student can explain atmospheric pressure, why it is lower at higher altitudes, and that it is measured with a barometer
Student can define wind as air moving from high to low pressure and name the wind vane and anemometer used for its direction and speed
visualIdeas: air moving from a high-pressure area to a low-pressure area
a wind vane

topics.title: Weather Instruments: Humidity
objectives: Student can define humidity as the amount of water vapour in the air and compare places like Kochi and Jaipur
Student can name the hygrometer as the instrument that measures humidity
visualIdeas: a coastal city and a desert city with water vapour icons

topics.title: Weather Stations
objectives: Student can explain how a weather station brings instruments together and how an Automated Weather Station works
Student can explain how an Automated Weather Station gives early warnings, as at a glacial lake in Sikkim
visualIdeas: a weather station enclosure with its instruments

topics.title: Predicting the Weather
objectives: Student can explain how meteorologists use long-term data to predict weather and why forecasts matter as extreme weather becomes more frequent
Student can read colour-coded weather warnings
visualIdeas: a weather warning map with colour codes

chapters.title: Climates of India
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Weather, Seasons and the Climate
objectives: Student can distinguish weather (short-term), seasons (recurring yearly) and climate (long-term patterns over decades)
Student can explain how seasons are related to both weather and climate
visualIdeas: a timeline from an hour to a year to decades

topics.title: Types of Climates in India
objectives: Student can describe the variety of climates in India, such as the alpine climate of the Himalayas
Student can match regions of India with their climates, such as subtropical northern plains, arid Thar and tropical wet west coast
visualIdeas: a climate map of India

topics.title: Factors Determining the Climate
objectives: Student can explain how latitude and altitude affect climate
Student can explain how proximity to the sea, winds and topography affect climate
visualIdeas: a hill station at high altitude and a coastal town by the sea
the Himalayas blocking cold winds

topics.title: The Monsoons
objectives: Student can explain that monsoons are seasonal winds caused by land and sea heating and cooling at different rates
Student can explain why the monsoon is central to life and agriculture in India
visualIdeas: summer and winter wind directions over India

topics.title: Climate and our Lives
objectives: Student can give examples of festivals and cultural practices linked to seasons and agriculture
Student can explain how climate affects the economy, for example through monsoon failure
visualIdeas: harvest festival scenes from different states

topics.title: Climates and Disasters
objectives: Student can describe cyclones, floods, landslides and forest fires and where they are common in India
Student can suggest ways to prepare for climate-related disasters
visualIdeas: icons of a cyclone, a flood, a landslide and a forest fire on a map of India

topics.title: Climate Change
objectives: Student can define climate change and explain how human activities such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation have driven it since the 19th century
Student can explain the terms mitigation, resilience and sustainable in the context of climate change
visualIdeas: a factory chimney and cut forest beside a rising thermometer

visualIdeas: an iron ploughshare and early silver punch-marked coins

visualIdeas: a chart of occupations in a complex society

topics.title: Developments Elsewhere in India

chapters.title: The Rise of Empires

objectives: Student can describe Mahmud of Ghazni's raids into north India after defeating the Hindu Shahis
Student can explain that scientific work continued in other regions, as with Bhaskaracharya
visualIdeas: a map of the Ghaznavid raids

topics.title: Eastern India
objectives: Student can describe the Sena dynasty that followed the Palas in the east
Student can describe the Eastern Gangas of Kalinga and the Senas' patronage of poets like Jayadeva
visualIdeas: a map of eastern India in the 11th century

topics.title: Further South
objectives: Student can describe the Kakatiyas, the Hoysalas and the Cholas as masters of the seas
Student can explain how the Kakatiyas and Hoysalas grew stronger as the Western Chalukyas faded
visualIdeas: Chola ships crossing to Southeast Asia
the Warangal fort gateway

topics.title: Back to the North
objectives: Student can describe the Paramaras of Malwa
Student can explain why the Ghurid conquest of Delhi and the Gangetic plains was a turning point
visualIdeas: a map of the Ghurid conquests

topics.title: Governance, Trade and Cultural Life
objectives: Student can describe how kingdoms kept armies and administrations, and how trade, art and literature continued to thrive
Student can explain why powerful kings needed efficient administrations to support large armies
visualIdeas: a temple and a trading port of the period

topics.title: Taking Stock
objectives: Student can summarise the changes and continuities of the 11th and 12th centuries
Student can explain that large parts of north India and all of south India remained outside Turkic rule in this period
visualIdeas: a change-and-continuity chart

chapters.title: India, a Home to Many
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: The Story of Indian Jews and the Syriac Christian Community
objectives: Student can describe how Jewish communities found a safe haven in India
Student can describe how Syriac Christian groups settled in India
visualIdeas: a synagogue and a church in Kerala

topics.title: The Legend of the Parsi Wise Man, Milk, and Sugar
objectives: Student can retell the legend of how the Parsis came to India and were welcomed
Student can explain why Zoroastrians left Persia after the 7th century and settled on India's western coast
visualIdeas: a bowl of milk with sugar dissolved in it

topics.title: The Arab Merchant Community and the African Connection
objectives: Student can describe how Arab merchants settled on the west coast
Student can describe the history of the Siddis of African origin in India
visualIdeas: a map of the west coast trading towns

topics.title: The Armenians and the Baha'i Community in India
objectives: Student can describe the Armenian merchants and the Baha'i community who made India their home
Student can explain why Baha'is came to India and what the faith teaches about unity
visualIdeas: the Lotus Temple

topics.title: The 'Good Maharaja' and the Polish Children
objectives: Student can retell how a Maharaja gave shelter to Polish children during the Second World War
Student can explain why a square in Warsaw honours the Maharaja of Nawanagar
visualIdeas: the Good Maharaja Square monument in Warsaw

topics.title: Tibetan Refugees in India
objectives: Student can describe how Tibetan refugees found a home in India
Student can describe how Buddhism spread to Tibet and the long links between India and Tibet
visualIdeas: a Tibetan settlement in the hills

topics.title: "The Whole World is Family" and Indian Values Beyond India
objectives: Student can explain values like vasudhaiva kutumbakam and atithi devo bhava that underlie India's acceptance of others
Student can describe how Indian communities abroad practise similar values
visualIdeas: a globe with people holding hands

chapters.title: The State, the Government, and You
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: What is a State? What is a Government?
objectives: Student can define a state and its four parts, and explain how the state differs from the government
Student can describe the government as the system that makes and enforces laws and resolves disputes
visualIdeas: a diagram of the state: territory, population, government, sovereignty

topics.title: Democracy and Republic
objectives: Student can explain the difference between a democracy, where people choose their government through free and fair elections, and a republic, where the head of state is elected and not hereditary
Student can explain why the Constitution uses 'democratic' and 'republic' together, and why some democracies such as the UK are not republics
visualIdeas: the Preamble with "democratic republic" highlighted

topics.title: India, a Republic that Protects the Rights of All
objectives: Student can explain how the Constitution and the law ensure that rule by a representative majority does not violate the fundamental rights of any citizen
Student can explain the 'dominance of the majority' using the example of a residents' association that banned deliveries after 9 pm
Student can give an example of rights protected by law, such as the Dongria Kondh tribe and their sacred hills
visualIdeas: a majority and a minority group with the Constitution as a shield between them

topics.title: Legislature: The Lawmaking Body
objectives: Student can explain the role of the legislature in making laws
Student can explain that states have their own legislatures that make laws for the state
visualIdeas: Parliament in session

topics.title: Executive: The Law-Implementing and Policymaking Body
objectives: Student can distinguish the political executive from the permanent executive

Student can describe how the permanent executive, civil servants selected through examinations such as those of the UPSC, implements laws and schemes, links citizens with the government and keeps records
visualIdeas: a chart of political and permanent executive

topics.title: The Government and You
objectives: Student can describe the government's triple role of protector, provider and regulator, with examples
Student can list ways citizens can get the government to act, such as grievance redressal, the Right to Information Act, the media, civil society organisations, writing to representatives and voting
Student can explain how citizens of Bagepalli used an RTI request to get roadwork completed properly
visualIdeas: a citizen's toolkit: grievance portal, RTI request, newspaper, NGO, letter and ballot

topics.title: Judiciary: Guardian of the Constitution
objectives: Student can explain what the judiciary does and why it is important for the rule of law
Student can explain why an independent judiciary keeps justice fair for all
visualIdeas: a court with scales of justice

topics.title: Tiers of Government
objectives: Student can describe the union, state and local tiers of government
Student can explain decentralisation
visualIdeas: three tiers stacked: union, state, local

chapters.title: Infrastructure: Engine of India's Development
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: Introduction: Why is Physical Infrastructure Important?
objectives: Student can explain what infrastructure is and why it matters for daily life and the economy
Student can trace how a journey or a farmer's produce depends on bridges, metros, railways, buses and phones
visualIdeas: a town with and without roads, power and water

topics.title: Transportation Infrastructure: Roads and Railways
objectives: Student can describe India's road and highway network and the Indian railway network
Student can explain why the British introduced railways in India in 1853 and how railways became a lifeline
visualIdeas: a highway and a railway line across a map of India

topics.title: Transportation Infrastructure: Metro, Air, Shipping and Ports
objectives: Student can describe metro systems, air transport, and shipping and ports, and what each is best suited for
Student can explain why ships are used for heavy goods and air transport for urgent or perishable goods
visualIdeas: a metro train, a plane and a cargo ship

topics.title: Communications Infrastructure
objectives: Student can describe the cables, towers, satellites and data centres that enable communication
Student can trace the journey of a voice note through towers, fibre cables and satellites
visualIdeas: a voice note travelling via towers and cables

topics.title: Collective Responsibility Towards Infrastructure
objectives: Student can explain why caring for public infrastructure is every citizen's responsibility
Student can suggest ways to improve services like waste management, traffic management and safe drinking water
visualIdeas: children cleaning a public park

chapters.title: Banks and the Magic of Finance
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: What are Banks and What Do They Do?
objectives: Student can describe savings, current and fixed deposit accounts
Student can explain how banks give loans and earn from the difference between interest on loans and on deposits
visualIdeas: money flowing from depositors to borrowers through a bank

topics.title: Other Financial Institutions
objectives: Student can describe financial services of post offices and institutions like NABARD
Student can explain the role of the Reserve Bank of India as the regulator
visualIdeas: a post office and the RBI building

topics.title: Payment Modes and Systems
objectives: Student can explain how cash is withdrawn and how money is transferred by cheque, debit card and UPI
Student can identify the parts of a cheque and explain how a cheque payment is debited and credited
visualIdeas: a cheque with its parts labelled
a UPI payment on a phone

topics.title: Stock Market
objectives: Student can explain that a share is part-ownership in a company and that the stock market is where shares are bought and sold
Student can explain that buying a share makes a person a part-owner of a company
visualIdeas: a company pie divided into shares
